podcast.title: Breakup Due to Alt Rock Decline
podcast.body: The band broke up in 2000, identified as "victims of a low in interest in 90s style alt rock." This suggests their sound fell out of fashion, contributing to their dissolution. "they were victims of a low in interest in 90s style alt rock, and they broke up in 2000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Major Label Deal and Japanese Release
podcast.body: After their indie success, The Gufs signed a major label deal and released two additional albums. All three of their albums were released in Japan, where the band unexpectedly developed a notable fan base. "The attention this album brought got them a major label deal, which resulted in two more albums. All three were released in Japan, for some reason, and a reasonable fan base there."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin and Early Indie Success
podcast.body: The Gufs originated from London, Ontario, and initially achieved success as an indie band. The attention garnered by their album *A Soap Bubble and a Nersia* led to them securing a major label deal. "From London, Ontario, the Gendarvis with pretty much their only hit, but it was a big one on the radio back then."

podcast.title: Paul Yego's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Singer Paul Yego is now a geologist residing in Nothing, Arizona, a town located in the northwest part of the state. He also maintains a musical project called Said Dog with his wife. "singer Paul Yego is now a geologist. He's living in Arizona. He was headquartered in a place, and I'm deadly serious about this, a place called Nothing Arizona."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the '90s: Part 1

xref.title: Paul Yego's Musical Project
xref.body: Said Dog is a musical project formed by Paul Yego, former singer of The Gufs, and his wife. This endeavor showcases his continued involvement in music, separate from his previous band. "He also has a musical project with his wife called Said Dog, and you can find them on Facebook."
